subject: Amanda Nunes
title: Is Amanda Nunes retired? No: she lost to Kayla Harrison at UFC 334
answer: No, not officially. Amanda Nunes retired in June 2023 but came back and challenged champion Kayla Harrison at UFC 334 on Nov. 14, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Harrison won by fourth-round submission. Nunes did not speak to reporters after the fight and has not announced a new retirement.
body:
Nunes, a former two-division UFC champion, gave up her title and stepped away after beating Irene Aldana by unanimous decision at UFC 289. She later said she had been burned out and needed time away from the pressure of title defenses. She re-entered the UFC's drug-testing pool in 2025, a required step for a return, and called for a fight with Harrison, her former training partner.

The bout was first planned for UFC 324 in January 2026 but was postponed after Harrison needed neck surgery. At UFC 334 in New York, Nunes had a strong start, but Harrison finished her with a rear-naked choke in the fourth round to keep the women's bantamweight title and improve to 20-1. Nunes left without giving a post-fight interview.

Before the fight, Nunes said that if she won she would have to "defend the belt," and "then we're going to see." UFC president Dana White said afterward that she looked good for someone coming back from three years off. Harrison was noncommittal about her own next step.
in_the_news: Amanda Nunes lost to Kayla Harrison by fourth-round submission at UFC 334 on Nov. 14, 2026, in her first fight in more than three years; she has not said whether she will fight again.
